method: Finite read-only source study; no upstream code execution, installation, build, game launch or public publication
scope: All non-transformer src/main Java, all src/mod Java/resources excluding META-INF/asm/*.js and coremods.json; plus main service descriptors

FFAPI modules: event/API emulation, dynamic registries, fluid render/variant attributes, object builder

Forge/ModLauncher/SecureJarHandler/Mixin/JDK internals: actual invocation order, injected target shapes, module behavior

facet_scope_assessment.boundary: Host and Fabric-fork resolver implementations remain external; declarations do not establish launch success
Forked Fabric setup, language adapters and final invocation implementation are external
Specific early holders, late snapshots/unfreeze and particle retention; no universal registry compatibility proof
Forge setup/register/attribute/HUD events are wired; full Fabric event emulation belongs to FFAPI and is not mapped from these files
Null flag, lazy handshake, duplicate pipeline guard and particle registry sync only; packet codec/channel compatibility unverified
Synthetic mixin hooks, mutable views, registry key adapters and late cache rebuilds; not a replacement renderer or full map API
Use-on scaffold and helpers preserve narrow contracts; general item/crafting semantics are not reimplemented
c-to-forge/vanilla naming heuristics and marked-pack language lookup, not semantic equivalence of arbitrary data
Category mutability/merge only, with insertion-order limitation; recipe serializers are not covered here
POI Holder-map mismatch, piglin currency dispatch and entity-attribute timing; goals/pathfinding are not implemented
Dynamic-registry resource path choice and injected registry detection; terrain/noise/biome algorithms are not implemented
Version-coupled reflective host/JDK internals and limited generated-package conventions
Explicit version/dist/input fingerprint and staged errors; environment-complete invalidation and runtime correctness are unverified
This inspected layer adapts external mods rather than defining its own gameplay catalogue; this does not mean corresponding interoperability facets are absent
